knowledge: Driver naming: a driver's full name is the forename plus the surname, and questions name drivers that way ("player" is used as a synonym for driver); the reference-name columns hold short reference names, and the qualified-lap periods are the first/second/third qualifying times (Q1/Q2/Q3).

Finish and lap readings: a result's time exists only when the driver finished the race (a missing time means not finished), and the time formats are lap-style 'M:SS.mmm' / 'MM:SS.mmm' or, for the race champion, 'H:MM:SS.mmm'; a lap time below a given duration is a comparison on the seconds; "best/shortest lap time" is the MIN time (resp. MIN milliseconds), "fastest lap speed" the MAX lap speed, and an average lap time the AVG of the milliseconds.

Result status readings: a disqualified driver is the disqualification status, accidents are counted via the accident status (status ids), and "ranked highest" means the smallest rank value (rank 1 is the best).

Naming of races, circuits and places: a question naming a Grand Prix means the race with that name; a race number is the race id; circuit coordinates are the latitude/longitude pair; a country can be named as a country or as a nationality, and language variants of a country name refer to the same country (Dutch = Netherlands).

Time readings: "in September 2005" is the month and year of the date; "from 2007 to 2009" and "between 1980 and 2010" are year ranges; "born before 1985" compares the birth year; "the earliest recorded year and month" is the MIN date's year and month; "the first race" is the minimum year.
Percentages put one set of the same entities on both sides of the fraction (count of entities satisfying the condition / count of entities in scope, times 100), counted once per entity.
